title: Trade and Its Blessings in Islam
summary: The discussion highlights the importance of trade in Islam, emphasizing that it brings blessings, self-reliance, and mental freedom. It points out that while reliance solely on Allah is suitable for those with strong faith, ordinary people should engage in trade and work as it is honored in Islam. Prophets like Solomon and David had wealth alongside their spiritual roles, showing that material endeavors do not conflict with faith. Islam promotes a balanced view on wealth, and diligent, honest trade is encouraged as it can lead to forgiveness of sins.
translation: Trade brings blessings along with self-reliance and mental freedom for a person. Keeping a beard, praying on time, and carrying out all duties are blessings of trade. Some people, despite having the ability to trade, engage only in religious acts, relying on Allah for sustenance. This reliance is suitable for those at high faith levels, while ordinary people should work and trade. Imam Abu Bakr al-Jassas stated that abandoning permissible activities doesn't lead to merit. Unlike other faiths, Islam is balanced in terms of wealth and considers it good. Those who disdain worldly trade may undervalue eternal rewards. Prophet Solomon and Prophet David showed that worldly gains don't detract from prophethood. Disparaging economic endeavors misinterprets Islam as monastic. The Quran encourages economic activity, though it's not purely economic. Engaging in trade leads to forgiveness of sins as per the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Hard work and seeking lawful earnings lead to forgiveness. A lowly trade is better than begging; earning enables spending. The Prophet (ﷺ) established a market in Medina for Muslim trade, ensuring high standards and avoiding prohibited items. Muslims are instructed to pray, work diligently, and seek God's help. Trade brings blessings, supports families, and offers a free life. May Allah grant us understanding and elevate Muslims in commerce.
